messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
version:3.1.0
IP:192.168.11.33
API name: get nodes list
Parameter_fabricName:PEK-ACI

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of nodes associated with a specified fabric in a network. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to. The URL should include the target IP, API endpoint, and the fabricName query parameter placeholder https://<ip>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName={fabricName}.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric whose nodes are to be listed. This value is used to replace the {fabricName} placeholder in the URL.

message.reasoning:
The user wants instructions on how to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. They provide version, IP, API name, and parameter. We need to respond with step-by-step instructions. Also we can use the function to actually make the request. But the question is about generating the request, not executing it. However we could show how to construct the URL and maybe call the function.

We have a tool function requests_get that takes url and fabricName. We can call it with the constructed URL. The default URL includes placeholder. We'll replace {fabricName} with PEK-ACI. So URL becomes https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI. Then we can call the function.

But the user didn't ask us to execute; they asked "How to generate a RESTful API request". So we should explain steps: open Nexus Dashboard, navigate to API section, choose API name, fill parameters, click Generate or Execute. Provide example URL. Optionally show how to use curl or Postman. And optionally demonstrate using our function.

Thus answer: Step 1: login to dashboard at https://192.168.11.33. Step 2: Go to API Explorer. Step 3: Select API "get nodes list" (or find under Telemetry). Step 4: Enter Parameter_fabricName as PEK-ACI. Step 5: Click Generate Request. It will produce URL: https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI. Step 6: Use curl: curl -k -X GET "https://192.168.11.33/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/nodes?fabricName=PEK-ACI" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" etc. Or use Postman.

Also mention authentication: token or basic auth. Provide sample code snippet.
